Motorists wading through the waterlogged 45-feet road at Balaji Nagar in Puducherry on October 25, 2026 | Photo Credit: S.S. Kumar
Heavy rain lashed Puducherry on Sunday (October 25, 2026), inundating low-lying neighbourhoods, flooding houses and disrupting normal life across the city.
Puducherry recorded 9.7 cm of rainfall between 5.30 p.m. on Saturday (October 24) and 8.30 a.m. on Sunday. Rainwater surged through major stormwater drains including the Grand Canal and Uppanar.
Waterlogging was reported in Boomianpet, Krishna Nagar and Venkata Nagar, with rainwater entering houses in some localities. The Indira Gandhi Square, Rajiv Gandhi Square and Sivaji statue junctions on the East Coast Road were inundated, slowing vehicular movement.
Rainwater being pumped out through a motor pump near 45 feet Road at Venkata Nagar in Puducherry on October 25, 2026 | Photo Credit: S.S. Kumar
Motorists struggled to negotiate flooded stretches as rains continued across the city. Many residents stayed indoors, while vendors at the Sunday Market on Mahatma Gandhi Road struggled to set up stalls, affecting business.
Meanwhile, distant cautionary signal No. 1 was hoisted at Puducherry port. The Department of Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare has advised Puducherry fishermen not to venture into the sea until October 27 in view of the likelihood of strong winds over the Bay of Bengal.
Motorists and pedestrians wade through waterlogged 45 Feet Road in Balaji Nagar and Venkata Nagar, Puducherry, on Sunday, October 25, 2026. Video: @SS_KUMAR2010 https://t.co/9mhuq83WFQ
In neighbouring Tamil Nadu, the Regional Meteorological Centre has forecast heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places in Cuddalore district and heavy rain at isolated places in Villupuram district on Sunday.
In Cuddalore, Collector Sibi Adhithya Senthil Kumar advised residents of low-lying areas and those living near waterbodies to move to safer locations when flood warnings were issued.
People were urged to avoid bathing in rivers and other waterbodies during heavy rain and to keep important documents, medicines and torches readily available.
The district’s round-the-clock emergency control room can be contacted on 1077 or 04142-220700. Fishermen in Cuddalore district have been instructed not to venture into the sea from October 25 to 29.
